input.recipient: Landlord of Flat 9, 59 Alder Lane, Eastmere
input.body:
Address: Flat 9, 59 Alder Lane, Eastmere, ZZ4 4ZZ
Ref: TKT-1B8B91

Hi,

The tenant of this property has reported the following. Can you please advise if you wish for me to instruct a contractor to attend or if you want to arrange your own contractor?

Request description: "Washing machine broken, it's LG , we have googled it, it has power failure and can't be fixed, I am willing to replace, this one was here when I moved in, but if I replace it will be mine and not become part of the property, if I ever was to move out I would take it with me."

As the machine was in the property when the tenant moved in, we understand it is a landlord-supplied appliance. Please note the tenant's view that it "can't be fixed" comes from an online search, not an engineer's diagnosis. Please let us know which option you prefer:
1. We instruct an appliance engineer from our panel to diagnose and repair (within our £250 pre-authorised limit; we will come back to you for approval if a repair or replacement costs more).
2. You arrange your own engineer or a replacement machine.
3. You accept the tenant's offer to buy and fit their own washing machine at their cost. It would belong to the tenant, they would take it with them when they leave, and it would not form part of the inventory. If you choose this, please confirm what you want done with the existing LG machine (removed and disposed of, or stored), and note the property would then have no landlord-supplied washing machine when this tenancy ends.

No photos have been received yet; we have asked the tenant for photos of the machine and any error codes.

Kind regards,
Resolve AI, Maintenance Team

input.recipient: Tenant of Flat 9, 59 Alder Lane, Eastmere
input.body:
Hello,

Thank you for reporting the problem with the LG washing machine (ref TKT-1B8B91). As the machine was in the property when you moved in, it belongs to the landlord. We have told the landlord and asked whether they want us to send an engineer, arrange their own repair or replacement, or accept your offer to fit your own machine, which you would keep and take with you when you move out.

Until the landlord confirms, please do not remove, throw away or replace the existing machine. We will let you know their decision as soon as we hear back.

In the meantime, please could you:
- send photos of the machine, including the display and any error codes;
- check the plug is fully in and the socket works (try another small appliance in it), and check whether the fuse in the plug or a trip switch on the consumer unit has gone.

If you notice any burning smell, sparking or smoke from the machine or socket, switch it off at the wall, do not use it, and tell us straight away.

Kind regards,
Resolve AI, Maintenance Team
